content:
The **Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery** is a Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC) burial site located near the village of **Beaumont-Hamel** in the **Somme department of northern France**. It is one of several cemeteries in the area commemorating soldiers who fought in the **Battle of the Somme (1916)**, particularly during the **First Day of the Somme (1 July 1916)**, one of the bloodiest days in British military history.

---

### **Key Facts About Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery**
#### **1. Location & Access**
- **Address:** Route de Mailly-Maillet, 80300 Beaumont-Hamel, France
- **Nearest Town:** Albert (about 10 km southeast)
- **Coordinates:** 50°04′38″N 2°39′11″E
- **Access:** The cemetery is located along the **D163 road** between Beaumont-Hamel and Auchonvillers, near the **Newfoundland Memorial Park** (a major WWI site).

#### **2. Historical Context**
- The cemetery was established **after the Armistice (1918)** when graves from the surrounding battlefields were concentrated here.
- It primarily contains soldiers who died during the **Battle of the Somme (1916)**, particularly in the **July–November 1916** offensive.
- Many of the burials are from the **29th Division**, which suffered heavy losses on **1 July 1916** (the first day of the Somme offensive).
- The **Royal Newfoundland Regiment** (part of the 29th Division) was nearly wiped out in the attack on **Beaumont-Hamel**, with **801 men killed, wounded, or missing** out of 865. Their sacrifice is commemorated at the nearby **Newfoundland Memorial Park**.

#### **3. Cemetery Details**
- **Number of Burials:** **1,329** (as per CWGC records)
  - **Identified Casualties:** **914** (British, Canadian, Australian, South African, and New Zealand soldiers)
  - **Unidentified Casualties:** **415** (mostly from the Somme battles)
- **Special Memorials:**
  - **18** soldiers are commemorated with **special memorials** because their graves were destroyed in later battles.
  - **1** soldier is commemorated on a **Duhallow Block** (a type of memorial for those whose graves were lost).
- **Design:**
  - Designed by **Sir Edwin Lutyens** (a famous architect of many CWGC cemeteries).
  - Features the **Cross of Sacrifice** and **Stone of Remembrance** (standard CWGC elements).
  - The cemetery is **rectangular** with **rows of white Portland stone headstones** set in well-maintained lawns.

#### **4. Notable Burials & Memorials**
- **Lieutenant Colonel Bernard Freyberg (VC, DSO)** – A New Zealand officer who later became **Governor-General of New Zealand (1946–1952)**. He was awarded the **Victoria Cross** for his actions at the **Battle of the Somme (1916)**.
- **Private William McFadzean (VC)** – An Irish soldier from the **Royal Inniskilling Fusiliers**, awarded the **Victoria Cross** posthumously for sacrificing himself to save comrades from a grenade explosion.
- **Many soldiers from the Newfoundland Regiment** – Though most Newfoundlanders are commemorated at the **Newfoundland Memorial Park**, some are buried here.

#### **5. Nearby Related Sites**
- **Newfoundland Memorial Park** – A preserved battlefield with trenches, memorials, and the **Caribou Monument** (symbol of the Newfoundland Regiment).
- **Y Ravine Cemetery** – Another CWGC cemetery nearby, containing many Newfoundlanders.
- **Hawthorn Ridge Crater** – A massive mine crater from the **1 July 1916** explosion (visible from the cemetery).
- **Thiepval Memorial** – The largest British war memorial in the world, commemorating **72,000 missing** from the Somme.
- **Auchonvillers Military Cemetery** – Another nearby CWGC site.

#### **6. Visiting Information**
- **Open:** Always accessible (CWGC cemeteries are open to the public year-round).
- **Best Time to Visit:** Spring to autumn (the Somme region is cold and wet in winter).
- **Facilities:** No visitor center, but information panels are present.
- **Guided Tours:** Many Somme battlefield tour companies include Beaumont-Hamel in their itineraries.
- **Nearby Accommodation:** Albert, Arras, and Amiens have hotels and B&Bs.

#### **7. Significance & Commemoration**
- The cemetery is a **place of pilgrimage** for British, Canadian, Australian, and New Zealand visitors, particularly descendants of those who fought in the Somme.
- **Remembrance ceremonies** are held here on **1 July** (anniversary of the Somme offensive) and **11 November** (Armistice Day).
- The **CWGC** maintains the cemetery, ensuring it remains a **dignified and peaceful** place of remembrance.

---

### **Why Is Beaumont-Hamel Important?**
- **Symbol of Sacrifice:** The Somme was one of the deadliest battles in history, with **over 1 million casualties** in 4.5 months.
- **Newfoundland’s Role:** The **Royal Newfoundland Regiment’s** near-destruction at Beaumont-Hamel is a key part of Canadian and Newfoundland military history.
- **Battlefield Preservation:** The area around Beaumont-Hamel is one of the best-preserved **WWI battlefields**, with trenches, shell craters, and memorials still visible.

---

### **Further Reading & Resources**
- **CWGC Website:** [Beaumont-Hamel British Cemetery](https://www.cwgc.org/find-a-cemetery/cemetery/61000/BEAUMONT-HAMEL%20BRITISH%20CEMETERY)
- **Newfoundland Memorial Park:** [Veterans Affairs Canada](https://www.veterans.gc.ca/eng/remembrance/memorials/overseas/first-world-war/france/newfoundland)
- **Books:**
  - *The First Day on the Somme* – Martin Middlebrook
  - *The Somme* – Peter Hart
  - *Newfoundland at the Somme* – Frank Gogos
